fit.gap_handling_summary: The outputs make a strong, credible case through Python, high-throughput APIs, fleet telematics, FastAPI templates, Kubernetes and observability. They do not fabricate Docker, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, EKS, EDI, query tuning or schema migrations. However, several must-have areas remain only partially evidenced, and the limited recent production coding is acknowledged only indirectly through internal tooling and the wish to return to hands-on work.

The senior-backend headline is reasonable, but the CV summary does not explicitly explain the deliberate director-to-IC transition; the cover letter does.
The second page contains only skills, languages and talks, leaving the two-page document poorly balanced.
The copied description "EuroPython-style conference talk" remains imprecise about the actual event, although it is faithful to the source.

evaluation.summary: These are credible, well-grounded application documents that reposition an engineering director toward hands-on backend work without rewriting the historical roles or inventing missing technologies. The strongest tailoring is the combination of Python/FastAPI, fleet-telematics ingestion, high-throughput APIs and operational reliability. Docker, CI/CD, REST consumption, query tuning and schema migrations remain unproven rather than falsely claimed, while the notes offer additional reassurance about title, salary and current technical focus that could have been used. The main presentation defect is the first employment heading/date collision, compounded by a dense first CV page and a sparsely filled second page. The notes contain a Munich remote/hybrid preference despite the separate preference field saying none was given; the outputs make no unsupported arrangement commitment, and the advertised EU-remote option creates no evident conflict.
